bib.title: Recursive Introspection: Teaching Language Model Agents How to Self-Improve

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only. Figure contents (Figs 4-10) not read, captions only.

question: Can a language model be fine-tuned so that it improves its own answer over sequential turns on a hard prompt, which prompted self-correction does not achieve in off-the-shelf models?
hypothesis: Fine-tuning on on-policy multi-turn rollouts, with improved responses supplied by best-of-N and a reward-weighted objective, instils a self-improvement capability that prompting alone cannot, because a sequence of conditionals can represent the target distribution with more flexibility than a single-turn model.
contributions: RISE: an iterative fine-tuning procedure that casts a single-turn prompt as a multi-turn MDP and trains on on-policy rollouts with improved next-turn responses.
Two supervision variants: distillation (responses from a more capable model, GPT-3.5) and self-distillation (best of N samples from the learner).
Reward-weighted (advantage-centred) regression objective that uses both successful and unsuccessful rollouts.
Two inference modes: with oracle (stop at first correct answer) and without oracle (majority vote over turns).

method.summary: Each training problem is turned into a multi-turn MDP in which the model's answer is followed by a fixed 'the answer is incorrect, try again' message. The current model is rolled out up to i turns at iteration i, and the response at the next turn is replaced by the best of 5 GPT-3.5 samples (distillation) or best of N=16 learner samples (self-distillation), chosen by answer correctness. The model is fine-tuned from the base on all data so far with a reward-weighted loss, after an initial 'knowledge boosting' SFT stage.
method.task: math reasoning with sequential self-correction (GSM8K, MATH; SVAMP out-of-distribution)

datasets.name: GSM8K
datasets.split: train portion used to generate trajectories each iteration; test held out

datasets.name: MATH
datasets.split: train portion used to generate trajectories; test held out

other.note: used only in the self-distillation experiment, Table 2; exact checkpoint not stated

other.use: expert sampling 5 responses per state (best by reward); also an evaluated Self-Refine baseline

training.objective: reward-weighted regression, max over theta of E sum_t log pi_theta(y_t|s_t) * exp(r_t/tau), modified to centre the exponentiated rewards around the per-prompt mean (advantage-weighted)
training.batch_size: per device 1, gradient accumulation 16, 4 GPUs (inferred: effective 64)

other.framework: FastChat codebase with the loss customised to be weighted by reward
other.tau: value of tau in Eq. 4.6 not stated
other.iterations_run: Llama2-7B: knowledge-boost stage then Iteration 1 and Iteration 2 (GSM8K and MATH); Mistral-7B: Iteration 1 only; self-distillation (Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B): one iteration only; authors say compute prevented more
other.iteration_init: each iteration starts from the base model and trains on data from all iterations so far, not continued from the previous checkpoint
other.knowledge_boosting: initial SFT on in-domain multi-turn rollouts generated from a capable model, before on-policy collection; size not stated
other.data_per_iteration: 1 trajectory per unique problem; at iteration i the current model is rolled out for at most i steps
other.supervision_distillation: GPT-3.5 given the conversation history, 5 responses sampled, the highest reward kept, ties broken arbitrarily
other.supervision_self_distillation: N=16 samples from the learner, best by reward

inference.samples: 5 turns; without oracle the answer at turn j is the majority vote over turns 1..j (maj@1 at turn 5 is 5 sequential samples); m5@t1 = majority of 5 parallel first-turn samples; number of runs or seeds not stated
inference.prompting: System prompt for step-by-step math with \boxed{} answer, one-shot example, then user turn 'The answer is incorrect. Please try again. Here's the question: <Query>' for each retry. Self-refine baseline uses a critique-then-rewrite one-shot prompt.

parameters.history_window: if turn j exceeds iteration k, only the most recent k interactions are kept to avoid test-time distribution shift
parameters.no_oracle_feedback: a fixed retry message that always says the answer is incorrect, regardless of correctness
parameters.with_oracle: rollout stops as soon as the answer checker says correct

other.serving: FastChat web API; one A100 or A40 per 7B model; GPT via OpenAI API

metrics.name: m1@t1
metrics.definition: maj@1, i.e. a single sample, at turn 1

metrics.name: m5@t1
metrics.definition: majority vote over 5 parallel samples at turn 1

metrics.name: m1@t5 (without oracle)
metrics.definition: run all five turns, majority vote over the candidates from turns 1..5

metrics.name: p1@t5 (with oracle)
metrics.definition: pass@1 at turn 5, stopping when the response is correct, so the verifier is queried after each turn

baselines: Self-Refine prompting (Llama2 variants, GPT-3.5, Mistral-7B, Eurus-7B-SFT)
GLoRE (numbers copied from its paper, no code)
V-STaR (Appendix B, numbers from its paper)
single-turn SFT on the same oracle data (correct only; correct and incorrect)
eval.protocol: Parenthesised deltas in Tables 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 are relative to m1@t1 (Table 5 caption). No seeds, error bars or significance tests reported for accuracies. Authors say comparisons to GLoRE, Eurus and V-STaR are not apples-to-apples.

prompts.purpose: RISE data generation and evaluation (GSM8K, MATH)
prompts.text: System: You are an AI language model designed to assist with math problem-solving. In this task, I will provide you with math problems. Your goal is to solve the problem step-by-step, showing your reasoning at each step. After you have finished solving the problem, present your final answer as \boxed{Your Answer}. <One-shot Example 16> User: <Query> Agent: <Answer> User: The answer is incorrect. Please try again. Here's the question: <Query> Agent: <Answer> ...

User: There is an error in the solution above because of lack of understanding of the question. What is the error? To find the error, go through each step of the solution, and check if everything looks good. Agent: <Critic> User: Now, rewrite the solution in the required format: Agent: <Refined Answer>

evidence.quote: Due to computational constraints, we were not able to perform more than two iterations of training with RISE, and no more than one iteration when the supervision comes from the learner itself.

results.claim: Llama2-7B trained with RISE (supervision from GPT-3.5 best-of-5), without oracle, gains 15.1 points at 5 turns after Iteration 1 and 17.7 after Iteration 2 on GSM8K, measured against its own turn-1 m1@t1.
results.baseline_value: 37.3 (m1@t1 at Iteration 2); base Llama2 11.1 at m1@t5
results.setup: GSM8K test, Llama2-7B-chat, RISE Iteration 2, no oracle, m1@t5 = majority vote over the 5 turns' candidates, temperature 1.0. Iteration 1: 35.6 to 50.7 (+15.1). Iteration 2: 37.3 to 55.0 (+17.7).
results.quote: RISE (“Iteration 1” and “Iteration 2”) boosts up the LLama2 base model’s five-turn performance by 15.1% and 17.7% respectively with each iteration on GSM8K and 3.4% and 4.6% on MATH, w/o any oracle.
results.note: The Table 1 caption says the biggest gain is between m5@t1 and m1@t5, but the 15.1 and 17.7 deltas are relative to m1@t1. Against m5@t1 (49.7 and 51.0) the 5-turn gains are only +1.0 and +4.0.

results.claim: With the oracle, Llama2-7B RISE reaches 63.9 (Iteration 1) and 68.4 (Iteration 2) pass@1 at turn 5 on GSM8K.
results.setup: GSM8K test, Llama2-7B, RISE Iteration 2, rollout stops once the answer checker says correct (verifier queried after every turn).

results.claim: GPT-3.5 with prompted Self-Refine on GSM8K: m1@t1 66.4; at turn 3 without oracle 61.0 (-5.4), with oracle 71.6 (+5.2). The paper reports only turn 1, turn 3 and (as a baseline row) turn 5 for GPT-3.5.
results.setup: GSM8K, GPT-3.5, one-shot Self-Refine critique-then-rewrite prompt (Fig 11), 3 turns, temperature 0.7. Columns: m1@t1 66.4, m5@t1 80.2 (+13.8), m1@t3 61.0 (-5.4) without oracle, p1@t3 71.6 (+5.2) with oracle. On MATH: 39.7, 46.5, 36.5 (-3.2), 46.7 (+7.0).
results.quote: Interestingly, we found using prompting-only self-refine [31] largely degrades performance across the board, even with a strong proprietary model, GPT-3.5.
results.note: There are no per-turn values for turns 2 and 4 for GPT-3.5. The p1@t3 figure (71.6) is a pass@1 with early termination on the oracle, not a self-contained improvement.
results.where: Table 1 and Table 6 (Appendix B.1), p10 and p24

results.claim: GPT-3.5 with the plain retry prompt (the 'Baselines' row, not Self-Refine) improves only 4.6 points over five turns without oracle on GSM8K, 8.3 with oracle.
results.setup: GSM8K, GPT-3.5, 5 turns, retry message prompt, temperature 0.7, majority vote over turns.
results.quote: In contrast, GPT-3.5 itself only improves by 4.6% over five turns.
results.table: Table 6, Baselines row GPT-3.5, columns m1@t5, p1@t5: 71.0 (+4.6), 74.7 (+8.3)
results.note: Its m5@t1 (80.6) is far higher than m1@t5 (71.0), so five turns of GPT-3.5 are worse than five parallel samples with a vote.

results.claim: Mistral-7B with RISE (Iteration 1) gains 23.9 points at 5 turns on GSM8K and 11.1 on MATH without oracle; Mistral-7B-Instruct alone gains 5.3 and 0.9.
results.setup: GSM8K 35.3 to 59.2; MATH 6.7 to 18.4; no oracle; GPT-3.5 supervision; one iteration.
results.table: Table 1, row + Iteration 1 (Mistral-7B), column m1@t5: GSM8K 59.2 (+23.9), MATH 18.4 (+11.1)

results.claim: Mistral-7B + RISE m1@t5 exceeds Eurus-7B-SFT on GSM8K.
results.setup: GSM8K, no oracle. Eurus has higher m1@t1 (36.3) and m5@t1 (66.3) than RISE Mistral (35.3, 50.6).
results.table: Table 1, row 7B SoTA Eurus-7B-SFT, column m1@t5: 47.9 (+11.6)

results.claim: Self-distillation RISE (supervision from the learner, N=16, one iteration, no boost stage) improves 5-turn maj@1 over turn 1 for Llama-3-8B and Mistral-7B but does not beat m5@t1.
results.setup: GSM8K, Llama-3-8B: 65.6 to 73.8 (+8.2), m5@t1 80.7; Mistral-7B: 36.8 to 39.5 (+6.6), m5@t1 44.4. Both no oracle.
results.quote: RISE improves the performance of LLaMa3-8B by 8.2% and Mistral-7B by 6.6%, entirely using their own data.

results.claim: Sequential 5-turn RISE (no oracle) beats 5 parallel first-turn samples with a vote, but by less than the quoted range for some cells.
results.setup: GSM8K (and MATH with Mistral-7B), equal sample count of 5.
results.quote: Comparing maj@5 performance at the end of 1 turn and 5 turns, we observe a consistent 4% to 8% improvement on GSM8K and an 6.5% improvement on MATH (with Mistral-7B model).
results.note: Table 1 gives Llama2 Iteration 1 as 50.7 vs 49.7 (+1.0), Iteration 2 as 55.0 vs 51.0 (+4.0), Mistral as 59.2 vs 50.6 (+8.6), and Mistral MATH as 18.4 vs 9.5 (+8.9, not 6.5), so the quoted range does not match every cell.

results.claim: Single-turn SFT on the same GPT-3.5 oracle data does not instil self-improvement.
results.setup: GSM8K, Llama2-7B, SFT on only correct oracle data: 27.4 to 34.0 (+6.6), m5@t1 42.2; SFT on correct and incorrect: 25.7 to 31.2. Both below RISE Iteration 1 (50.7).
results.quote: This means that the algorithmic design of RISE is critical in enabling it to learn self-improvement capabilities, as opposed to simply the use of expert supervision.
results.table: Table 1, rows SFT on oracle data, Only correct data: 27.4, 42.2 (+14.9), 34.0 (+6.6), 43.6 (+16.2)

results.claim: Out-of-distribution: RISE trained on MATH raises GSM8K m1@t5 to 32.6 (base 11.1); RISE trained on GSM8K reaches SVAMP m1@t5 50.0 (base 30.5), but MATH only 4.4 from GSM8K training.
results.setup: Llama2-7B, Iteration 1, no oracle, GSM8K test after MATH training.
results.table: Table 3, row Iteration 1 RISE Model trained on MATH (GSM8K), column m1@t5: 32.6 (+13.3)
results.note: MATH-from-GSM8K gain is only +0.1 without oracle (4.3 to 4.4).

results.claim: Weak-to-strong: Mistral-7B trained on rollouts from Llama2-7B reaches 62.7 m1@t5, above the 59.2 from its own rollouts; the reverse hurts Llama2 (45.2 vs 50.7).
results.table: Table 5, row + Iteration 1 (Llama2-7B) under Mistral-7B, column m1@t5: 62.7 (+24.5)

results.claim: Appending a novel correct response after successful rollouts gives the best Llama2 result; repeating the same correct response hurts.
results.setup: GSM8K, Llama2-7B Iteration 1 data modified. Repeating a correct response: 46.2.
results.table: Table 4, row +Appending a different correct response, column m1@t5: 51.1 (+18.0)

results.claim: Without oracle, Self-Refine prompting degrades Llama2 RISE models and open models at turn 3, e.g. Mistral-7B -12.5 and Eurus-7B-SFT -10.1 on GSM8K.
results.setup: GSM8K, Self-Refine prompt, 3 turns; Mistral-7B 33.7 to 21.2; Llama2 RISE Iteration 2 37.3 to 33.3 (-4.0).
results.quote: However, our experiments show that without any oracle hint from the environment or human feedback, the self-refine approach leads to a degradation in performance across all models.

results.claim: RISE (3-turn) gains 13.4 points without oracle against GLoRE's 3.4 over two turns.
results.source: GLoRE (Havrilla et al. 2024), numbers copied from its paper
results.setup: GSM8K; different base model, data and eval from RISE; no code available for GLoRE.
results.quote: RISE’s capabilities is particularly noteworthy considering that GLoRE utilizes 3 independent models
results.note: The passage reads 'sequentially enhancing its performance by an impressive 13.4% within just 3 turns without an oracle feedback, and by a remarkable 23.4% with an oracle'.

results.claim: RISE handles noisy feedback: with a verifier that always says the answer is wrong, the model still outputs correct answers in 3 of 4 later turns on one example.

limits: Authors: compute allowed no more than two RISE iterations, and only one when supervision comes from the learner itself; self-distilled RISE does not beat m5@t1.
Authors: RISE needs manual iterations; a fully online RL variant is suggested as future work.
Authors: fine-tunes one task at a time; mixing into general instruction tuning is untested.
Math reasoning only (GSM8K, MATH, SVAMP). Authors expect it would only incentivise hallucination on knowledge-based QA.
Comparisons with GLoRE, Eurus-7B-SFT and V-STaR differ in base model, data and eval setup; GLoRE and V-STaR numbers are copied from their papers.
No seeds, repeats or confidence intervals reported for accuracy; temperature 1.0 sampling.
The no-oracle protocol gives the model a message that always says 'incorrect'; the 'oracle' mode is not realistic where no checker exists, and the oracle supplies the stopping signal.
The knowledge-boost data size, tau, optimizer and total tokens are not stated; code and weights are not mentioned.

Internal inconsistency: Section 6.1.1 text says 4% to 8% and 6.5% on MATH but Table 1 cells give other values; Appendix B.1 says '3 iterations' for the V-STaR comparison while main text reports two RISE iterations after boosting.

terms.definition: the rollout terminates as soon as the response is correct, which queries the answer checker after each turn
full-length rollouts forcing retry, with a majority vote over all response candidates from turns 1..j
an initial phase of supervised fine-tuning on in-domain multi-turn rollouts from a capable model to give style and instruction-following information

lineage.work: Large language models cannot self-correct reasoning yet (Huang et al.)
lineage.note: RISE shows intrinsic self-improvement can be induced by fine-tuning; follows its error-analysis protocol
multi-model refinement; numbers from its paper
majority voting used for no-oracle answers
online imitation learning inspiration for on-policy rollouts
trains a separate corrector; at most two turns

figures.caption: Recursive Introspection (RISE). Using iterative multi-round training on on-policy rollouts and supervision from a reward function, RISE trains models that are capable of improving themselves over multiple turns.
figures.why: shows the whole training and majority-vote inference loop at a glance

figures.caption: RISE Inference. There are two ways to query the model trained via RISE upon inference: with oracle or without oracle.
figures.why: separates the two inference modes, the key to reading every table

figures.caption: RISE vs. other approaches (Self-Refine, GLoRE) and baselines.
figures.why: main results with and without oracle

figures.caption: Left: importance of data sources. Right: RISE with oracle error feedback to parallel sampling of 5 responses at turn 1.
